predictions.prediction_text: Oil prices will be pushed above $90-95 due to destabilisation of the Middle East and damaged supply chains.
predictions.expected_result: Brent or WTI closes above $90 and sustains levels near or above $95 within the coming weeks following escalation in the Persian Gulf.

predictions.prediction_text: Geo-risk premium on oil and gas products has spiked by as much as 50% (implying materially higher near-term prices while transit remains disrupted).
predictions.expected_result: Market-implied risk premium measures (e.g., oil forward curve spreads or volatility) increase by up to ~50% versus pre-disruption baselines while Gulf transit disruptions persist.

predictions.prediction_text: I expect the Iranian aggression to peak around the OPEX week with heightened market disruption.
predictions.expected_result: Risk assets and energy prices show peak volatility and directional moves coinciding with the specified OPEX week (measurable increase in realised or implied volatility).

predictions.prediction_text: In the second half of the year the Japanese government will no longer tolerate a persistently weak yen, creating left-tail carry-trade risk.
predictions.condition: in the second half of the year
predictions.expected_result: JPY strength manifests as a sustained appreciation versus major crosses (e.g., USD/JPY down materially) and periods of sharp yen jumps that cause losses for carry-trade positions.

predictions.prediction_text: Signs of delays and overspending at NVIDIA will be visible and act as a leading indicator of the AI bubble's end.
predictions.expected_result: NVIDIA reports operational delays or increased capital/expenditure guidance and the stock declines meaningfully (e.g., >10% from recent levels) following such disclosures.

predictions.prediction_text: Wall Street is expecting slippage and slowdown at TSMC in the second quarter, which when realised will contribute to the AI bubble bursting.
predictions.expected_result: TSMC reports revenue or shipment slippage in the second quarter and the stock declines materially, coinciding with broader sector weakness.

predictions.prediction_text: Gulf states have halted put trading on exchanges until Tuesday, indicating suppressed downside hedging and potential for abrupt repricing when resumed.
predictions.expected_result: Resumption of put trading is followed by increased demand and a spike in put prices/volatility, producing abrupt downward repricing in regional oil-linked assets.

predictions.prediction_text: If a Saudi refinery or the Petroline pipeline is hit, it could slow oil price increases but generate a spike in gas prices.
predictions.condition: if refinery or Petroline pipeline is hit
predictions.expected_result: Upon confirmed damage to the refinery or Petroline, regional/national gas prices (LNG/JET/industrial gas) spike sharply (measured >20% intraday/short-term rise) while oil price reaction differs (temporary moderation or localized impact).

predictions.prediction_text: Geopolitical tensions will seemingly ease slightly during the summer, reducing immediate market stress before the next critical window in November.
predictions.expected_result: Measured geopolitical risk indicators and market volatility decline through the summer months compared with spring levels, then rise again approaching November.

predictions.prediction_text: Markets are likely to 'wake up' to longer-term effects of geo risk toward the end of next week, reversing the current short-term suppression.
predictions.expected_result: Market realised/implied volatility and risk premia increase materially by the end of next week compared to intraday/early-week levels, with directional moves in risk assets reflecting reassessment of geo risk.
